subject.title: Synchronous crypto.createHash blocks Node.js event loop on large MCP schemas

question: Should maintainers treat the source-level synchronous bundle-MCP config hash as enough to queue a fix now, or require a focused reproduction that distinguishes large launch config from large returned tool schemas first?
rationale: Source proves synchronous hashing exists, but the issue's concrete schema example maps to another runtime path and the best fix changes depending on which payload blocks the Gateway.

options.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
options.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large mcp.servers config or returned tools/list schemas cause the Gateway heartbeat failure before queueing repair.

options.title: Queue Config-Hash Repair
options.body: Treat the synchronous bundle-MCP config hash as sufficient source proof and repair that path with focused event-loop-delay coverage.

options.title: Split Schema Catalog Follow-Up
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to launch-config hashing and open a separate schema-catalog issue only after a returned-schema repro is provided.

recommendation.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
recommendation.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large mcp.servers config or returned tools/list schemas cause the Gateway heartbeat failure before queueing repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete has the strongest current path history for bundle-MCP CLI config generation, while the decision can route schema-catalog work to adjacent MCP runtime owners if the repro points there.
